subject: SLA remedy formula clarification & baseline uptime request

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify monthly remedy calc and baseline uptime in SLA template

Hi Marissa / team,

Thanks for sending over the SLA template yesterday. Procurement and our ops team have two related asks before we can proceed to procurement review:

1) Baseline uptime: we need clarification on whether Redwood will consider a 99.98% availability baseline for the "payments-critical" workload we outlined. Our tolerance for interruptions on that flow is much tighter than other product traffic.

2) Monthly remedy calculation: the current formula in section 4.2 uses a flat % of monthly fees per uptime band. Can you confirm if you’re open to switching to a minutes-based formula (minutes of downtime * (monthly fee / minutes in month) * multiplier) so the remedy scales more directly with observed downtime?

Attached is a short spreadsheet from our finance team that shows how we model remedies for other vendors (monthly-remedy-calculation.xlsx).

If possible, can we get a short note on both points by end of week? We have an internal review on Monday.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Clarify monthly remedy calc and baseline uptime in SLA template

Felix — appreciate the clear asks and the spreadsheet. Quick summary of our starting position and what we can consider: 

- Baseline uptime: Redwood’s standard hosted availability is 99.95% (measured per calendar month, excluding maintenance carveouts). For dedicated/prod-critical workloads we do offer negotiable service bands. 99.98% is a meaningful step up in operational commitment and would typically require either a Dedicated pool or a Reserved capacity baseline. We can discuss mapping your "payments-critical" traffic to a dedicated pool as an option — this is the usual approach to hit 99.98.

- Remedy formula: we’re open to a minutes-based calculation. Our legal and finance teams typically prefer the remedy expressed as: monthly_remedy = min(cap, (downtime_minutes / minutes_in_month) * monthly_recurring_fee * multiplier). The multiplier is usually 1.5 for the first band, 2.0 for larger outages, etc. Cap is normally 100% of the monthly fee.

I’ve attached an edited SLA draft (sla-draft-nimbus_v2.pdf) that:
- Adds a clause for a "Dedicated payments baseline" option that can be selected in Schedule A,
- Replaces the flat-percentage table with a minutes-based formula and placeholders for multiplier values,
- Keeps the default cap at 100% but flags it as negotiable.

Next steps: Laura will drop in redlines around wording for carveouts/force majeure and maintenance. If you can confirm whether you want us to price Dedicated capacity for the payments workload (ballpark GPU hours / qps), we’ll include a commitment amendment to lock in 99.98.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that’s faster.

—Marissa

Folks — 

I reviewed the draft and wanted to call out three legal points to avoid later disputes:

1) Measurement window: define "minutes of downtime" with precise monitoring signals (e.g., token-level request failures vs. partial degradation). We recommend Redwood commit to the monitoring sources (internal telemetry + customer-facing health endpoint) with an agreed reconciliation process.

2) Maintenance carveouts: clarify scheduled maintenance windows and an advance-notice requirement (72 hours for non-emergency, 1 hour for critical patches). Also include a clause for emergency maintenance but require post-event report.

3) Cap mechanics and mitigation: instead of an unconditional 100% cap, propose a tiered cap for hosted: 50% for single-month severe outages, 100% only where Dedicated capacity is purchased. This aligns remedy visibility with operational levers.

I’ve added inline redlines in sla-draft-nimbus_v2.pdf (see attached) and marked the sections that will require commercial escalation if Nimbus needs the higher uptime without Dedicated.

Laura Bennett
Lead Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: Felix Ortega <felix@nimbus-payments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify monthly remedy calc and baseline uptime in SLA template

Hi all — thanks for the fast responses. A few clarifications from our side after a short sync with finance/ops:

- We understand Redwood’s default is 99.95. The payments-critical flow must be 99.98 or better. We are prepared to accept a Dedicated capacity addendum and incremental monthly fee for that pool; can you provide a ballpark delta (monthly) for the workload we described (~1500 qps peak, steady-state 800 qps, average request size small)?

- On the remedy cap: Nimbus prefers the principle that credits should be meaningful even for hosted customers. Would Redwood consider a 75% per-month cap for hosted (so not full 100%) and 100% only when Dedicated is contracted? That feels like a fair middle ground.

- For the minutes-based formula, finance wants explicit band multipliers. Proposed bands (by downtime minutes per month):
  - 0-5 min: 0x (no credit)
  - 6-60 min: 1.5x
  - 61-240 min: 2.0x
  - >240 min: 3.0x

If you can get a quick cost delta for Dedicated and confirm whether Redwood would accept a 75% hosted cap with the minutes-based formula, we can move to legal procurement next week.

Thanks — Felix
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify monthly remedy calc and baseline uptime in SLA template

Felix — super helpful, thanks. Short answers and next steps: 

1) Dedicated delta: we’ll run a quick capacity check with infra and send ballpark monthly pricing by EOD (expect a single-digit percentage premium over your current estimate for hosted, depending on region and reserved GPU hours). Karthik — can you drop a 1-page capacity note + ballpark pricing?

2) Hosted cap: Redwood can accept a 75% per-month cap for hosted customers for this deal — conditioned on acceptance of the minutes-based formula and the monitoring/reconciliation language Laura suggested. We’ll flag the 100% cap as available only when Dedicated is selected.

3) Band multipliers: the bands you proposed look reasonable. We’ll plug them into the SLA template exactly as listed.

Next steps: 
- Karthik to send capacity/price note (by 3pm PST today)
- I’ll circulate a redlined SLA with the minutes formula, the 75% hosted cap, and Laura’s monitoring language for final review
- If Nimbus is good, Laura and Nimbus counsel can exchange redlines and we can move to DocuSign.

Would you like a 30-min call this afternoon to walk the numbers? If not, we’ll proceed over email.

Regards,
